patterns.condition: Designing a wave or tower defense map
patterns.action: Build one loop: place or upgrade with the money you have, start the wave, enemies advance, kills pay out, survive, repeat harder. Every pass must make the next one possible.
patterns.statement: Defense depth comes from a planning loop, not from reflexes

patterns.condition: Writing the wave logic in Verse
patterns.action: Keep waves in an array of entries (enemy type, count, gap in seconds, reward) and loop over it, so balancing means editing numbers and never rewriting the manager.

patterns.condition: Tuning wave strength against the player economy
patterns.action: Check each wave with one number: total enemy health against the damage your defense deals while they cross the lane. Raise health faster than income and re-check after every price change.
patterns.statement: Enemy health must outgrow income and damage or the late game is trivial

patterns.condition: Playtests show everyone builds the same thing
patterns.action: Give each tower type a job (single target, area, slow, support) and a weakness another type covers, and cap the strongest one by cost or by count.
patterns.statement: One best tower makes every run identical

patterns.action: Use turret, guard and creature style devices for combat and spawning. Use Verse for waves, money, lives and win or lose, reading their spawn and elimination events.
patterns.statement: Let stock devices do the fighting and Verse do the rules

patterns.condition: Placement can change or block the enemy route
patterns.action: Reject any placement that would fully block the route, or keep the route fixed with barriers the player cannot move or remove.
patterns.statement: A player who can wall off the goal breaks the game

patterns.condition: A new enemy type or a boss is about to appear
patterns.action: Show the next wave before it starts (type, count, countdown) and introduce a new enemy alone in an easy wave first.

patterns.condition: Deciding what a leaked enemy costs
patterns.action: Make a leak cost lives and also the income it would have paid, so ignoring the defense never pays off.
patterns.statement: A leak that costs only lives is easy to ignore

patterns.action: Alternate: a rest wave after a hard one, a spike every few waves, and a rule changing wave (fast, armored, flying) so the build has to adapt.
patterns.statement: A difficulty line that only rises is dull

patterns.condition: Money or lives are tracked for each player in co-op
patterns.action: Hold money and score in a map keyed by player, change it only from events, and add a shared team pool when the design says everyone pays together.
patterns.statement: Per player state belongs in one map keyed by player

patterns.condition: Offering an endless or survival mode
patterns.action: Give endless waves a scaling cap or a milestone reward every few waves, so players see progress and know where failure comes from.
patterns.statement: Endless modes hide the real balance

patterns.condition: Preparing to publish a wave map
patterns.action: Play wave one to the last wave once with the real player count, note the wave where money runs short, and fix that wave before anything else.
patterns.statement: Play the whole curve before release
